title: Generate synthetic Langmuir isotherm data and fit models
action: Using the known Langmuir parameters (M=1, K_A=2, K_B=10, K_C=20), generate synthetic pure-component adsorption isotherm data for fictitious gases A, B, and C at a range of pressures. Then fit Langmuir models to each dataset using pyIAST's ModelIsotherm to obtain functional forms for the IAST calculation.
description: Preparation step: create the pure-component isotherm models required for the ternary IAST prediction.

title: IAST predictions for ternary Langmuir mixture
action: Using the fitted Langmuir models for A, B, and C, run pyIAST.iast() for a grid of gas compositions (mole fractions of A, B, C that sum to 1, e.g., step 0.1) at total pressure 1 bar. Compute and record the predicted loadings of A, B, and C for each composition.
description: CSV with columns: xA (gas mole fraction of A), xB, xC, predicted_loading_A, predicted_loading_B, predicted_loading_C (all mmol/g). One row per composition.
output_schema: Columns: xA (float, mole fraction of A in gas), xB (float), xC (float), predicted_loading_A (float, mmol/g), predicted_loading_B (float), predicted_loading_C (float). The sum of xA+xB+xC = 1.

title: Characterize pure-component isotherms for methane and ethane (IRMOF-1)
action: Load the methane and ethane pure-component isotherm CSV files (IRMOF-1_methane_isotherm_298K.csv and IRMOF-1_ethane_isotherm_298K.csv). Create InterpolatorIsotherm objects for methane and ethane using linear interpolation with fill_value set to the maximum loading observed in each dataset.
description: Preparation step: build the interpolation-based isotherm models needed for binary IAST and reverse IAST.

title: IAST binary methane/ethane predictions
action: Using the InterpolatorIsotherm objects for methane and ethane, run pyIAST.iast() for a range of gas-phase ethane mole fractions (y_ethane from 0 to 1, e.g., step 0.05) at total pressure 65 bar. Record the predicted loadings of methane and ethane and the total loading for each y_ethane.
description: CSV with columns: y_ethane (gas mole fraction of ethane), predicted_loading_CH4 (mmol/g), predicted_loading_C2H6 (mmol/g), total_loading (mmol/g).
output_schema: Columns: y_ethane (float, 0-1), predicted_loading_CH4 (float, mmol/g), predicted_loading_C2H6 (float, mmol/g), total_loading (float, mmol/g). One row per y_ethane.

title: Reverse IAST for methane/ethane
action: Using the same InterpolatorIsotherm objects, run pyIAST.reverse_iast() for a range of desired adsorbed-phase ethane mole fractions (x_ethane from 0 to 1, e.g., step 0.05) at total pressure 65 bar. Record the required gas-phase ethane mole fraction and the resulting predicted loadings.
description: CSV with columns: x_ethane (desired adsorbed mole fraction of ethane), required_y_ethane (required gas mole fraction), predicted_loading_CH4 (mmol/g), predicted_loading_C2H6 (mmol/g).
output_schema: Columns: x_ethane (float, 0-1), required_y_ethane (float, 0-1), predicted_loading_CH4 (float, mmol/g), predicted_loading_C2H6 (float, mmol/g). One row per x_ethane.

title: Characterize pure-component isotherms for CO2, N2, H2O (AX-21)
action: Load the CO2.csv, N2.csv, and H2O.csv files. For CO2, fit a Langmuir model using pyIAST.ModelIsotherm. For N2, fit a Henry's law model. For H2O, create an InterpolatorIsotherm with fill_value equal to the maximum H2O loading. These models will be used for the ternary IAST calculation.
description: Preparation step: build the isotherm models required for the ternary CO2/N2/H2O prediction.

title: IAST ternary CO2/N2/H2O prediction
action: Using the isotherm models for CO2 (Langmuir), N2 (Henry), and H2O (InterpolatorIsotherm), run pyIAST.iast() with the partial pressures: CO2 = 0.166 bar, N2 = 0.679 bar, H2O = 0.020 bar. Record the predicted loadings of CO2, N2, and H2O.
description: CSV with single row: predicted_loading_CO2, predicted_loading_N2, predicted_loading_H2O (all mmol/g).
output_schema: Columns: predicted_loading_CO2 (float, mmol/g), predicted_loading_N2 (float, mmol/g), predicted_loading_H2O (float, mmol/g). One row.
